statement.text:
A knot in $S^{3}$ bounds a topological disk in $B^{4}$ by coning (not
necessarily locally flat); this problem asks about topological disks that a knot in a
homology sphere $Y$ might bound in a homology or homotopy ball bounded by $Y$ .
(a) Given a locally flat knot in an integer homology 3-sphere, is it concordant
to a knot in $S^{3}$, via a locally flat annulus in a topological integer homology
cobordism? Variation: Can the homology cobordism be taken to be simply
connected?
(b) Given an arbitrary knot in an integer homology 3-sphere $Y$ , does it bound
an embedded disc (not necessarily locally flat) in $\Delta$, the Freedman filling
of $Y$ ? Variation: Is there such a disk in a homology ball bounded by $Y$ ?
(c) Is there a link in an integer homology 3-sphere, each of whose components
is independently concordant to a knot in $S^{3}$, that is not itself concordant
to a link in $S^{3}$.
(d) Suppose that $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ acts semi-freely on the homology sphere $Y$ , with fixed
point set a knot $K$. Does the action of $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ extend semi-freely over $\Delta$?
